answer: Consider a bonded-identity registry: before an AI agent may vote or claim rewards it must lock a real economic stake, and duplicates get slashed. The bond is charged per identity, so splitting one budget into a thousand Sybil accounts costs a thousand separate bonds, not one. With slashing, each forged persona also risks total forfeiture, so an attacker pays N times the stake and gambles it all on evasion. That scarce stake, counted in shale, crystal, or marble credits, is a per-identity toll that makes pseudonyms linearly expensive while honest agents post just one bond.
